title: Bone marrow, spleen and tumor collection for flow cytometry analysis
author: Javier Rodríguez-Baena
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.kjecuje
materials: Add 7AAD (1:100) and blocking 2.4G2 (1:100) solutions in FACS buffer in a total volume of 50µL and pipette vigorously. Incubate 5 minutes on ice.

Add the antibodies to the incubated tube (1:50 in a total volume of 50 µL to use them at a final dilution of 1:100 in a total volume of 100µL) and incubate 25 minutes on ice. 50µL of FACS buffer without antibody will be added to the negative control tube.

steps.title: Euthanize and disinfect animal
steps.instruction: Kill the mouse by cervical dislocation, then spray the whole animal with 70 % ethanol. Allow up to 30 min for the dissection steps.

steps.title: Make ventral midline incision and remove skin
steps.instruction: Make a ventral midline incision from the hips to the tail, cut laterally to both legs, remove as much skin and fur as possible, and peel the animal from the hips down.

steps.title: Harvest hind legs and preserve in PBS
steps.instruction: Cut both legs at the hipbones, place each leg in a 15 mL conical tube with enough sterile PBS to fully cover the tissue, keep on ice and avoid drying; legs can be stored for several hours.

steps.title: Expose femur and tibia
steps.instruction: Place each leg in a 100 mm or 150 mm tissue‑culture plate and remove the flesh covering the femur and tibia using forceps, scissors or a scalpel.

steps.title: Separate femur and tibia and cut ends
steps.instruction: Twist and pull the femur away from the knee and tibia with forceps to avoid fracture, then cut off the metaphysis and epiphysis (head of femur and knee end) with strong scissors to expose the red, rounded marrow cavity.

steps.title: Flush bone marrow with PBS
steps.instruction: Hold the bone by its mid‑shaft, draw 1–2 mL sterile PBS into a 2 mL syringe fitted with a 23 G needle, inject into the shaft, bend the dish to collect the flow, and repeat 3–4 times until the shaft appears white; the PBS will turn reddish as marrow is released.

steps.title: Filter marrow suspension through 100 µm strainer
steps.instruction: Disaggregate the flushed material by moving the syringe up and down, then filter the homogenised PBS‑marrow mixture into a 50 mL conical tube using a 100 µm cell strainer.

steps.title: Repeat flushing for second leg
steps.instruction: Perform the same flushing procedure on the opposite leg, adding a few millilitres of fresh PBS as needed to prevent drying.

steps.title: Centrifuge bone marrow cells
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the combined marrow suspension at 300 g for 5 min at room temperature.

steps.title: Resuspend in DMEM and count cells
steps.instruction: Resuspend the pellet in 10 mL DMEM, count cells with a Neubauer hemocytometer, and adjust to ~4 × 10⁵ cells · mL⁻¹ for plating in petri dishes or multi‑well plates as required.

steps.title: Extract spleen and place in cold collagenase
steps.instruction: Take a ventral midline incision, remove the spleen and trim away fat; if part of the spleen is needed for other assays, cut it with a scalpel and keep at least half of the organ in 1 mL cold collagenase in a 15 mL conical tube on ice (preserves for several hours at 4 °C).

steps.title: Mechanically dissociate spleen on 70 µm strainer
steps.instruction: Place a 70 µm cell strainer on a sterile bacterial plate, put the spleen on the strainer (no media), and crush it with the plastic plunger of a 3 mL syringe, triturating until only connective tissue remains on the strainer.

steps.title: Rinse strainer with cold collagenase
steps.instruction: Rinse the strainer and plate with 1 mL cold collagenase (the same used to store the spleen), collect the rinse into a 50 mL conical tube, then repeat with another 1 mL cold collagenase; keep the tube on ice until all spleens are processed.

steps.title: Enzymatic digestion of spleen cells
steps.instruction: Incubate the collected cell suspension at 37 °C for 1 h, shaking gently every 10 min to promote enzymatic disaggregation.

steps.title: Add RPMI‑10 and filter through 70 µm strainer
steps.instruction: Add 3 mL RPMI‑10 to the digested suspension, pass the mixture through a 5 mL syringe fitted with a 19.5 G needle 3–4 times, then filter it through a fresh 70 µm cell strainer placed in a new 50 mL conical tube.

steps.title: Centrifuge spleen cell suspension
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the filtered suspension at 300 g for 5 min.

steps.title: Lyse red blood cells with ACK buffer
steps.instruction: Discard the supernatant, resuspend the pellet in 5 mL Red Blood Cell Lysis Buffer (ACK), and incubate for 4 min at room temperature.

steps.title: Centrifuge after lysis
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the lysed suspension at 300 g for 10 min.

steps.title: Resuspend in DPBS and count cells
steps.instruction: Remove the supernatant and resuspend the pellet in 5–10 mL DPBS (volume depends on whether the original spleen was half or whole); count viable cells using trypan blue.

steps.title: Excise tumor tissue without surrounding fat
steps.instruction: Remove the tumor mass, taking care not to include any skin, connective tissue, or fat.

steps.title: Mechanically mince tumor tissue
steps.instruction: On a clean cell‑culture plate, finely chop the tumor with small scissors or a blade to obtain a smooth tissue slurry (caution advised).

steps.title: Prepare cell suspensions for FACS staining
steps.instruction: Adjust each cell suspension to 1 × 10⁶ cells per FACS tube; allocate 2 tubes for triple‑color panels (CD3‑CD45R‑CD11b and CD11b‑F4/80‑Gr1), 5 tubes for single‑color stains (CD3, CD45R, CD11b, F4/80, Gr1), and 1 tube as an unstained negative control.

steps.title: Centrifuge stained cells
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the stained cell suspensions at 300 g for 5 min.

steps.title: Wash cells with FACS buffer
steps.instruction: Add 1 mL FACS buffer to each pellet, then centrifuge again at 300 g for 5 min.

steps.title: Resuspend stained cells for flow cytometry
steps.instruction: Without pipetting, gently resuspend each pellet in 500 µL FACS buffer; the samples are now ready for flow‑cytometry analysis.
